label: Brisnik A7: fluoxetine, paroxetine or bupropion with metoprolol or propranolol
title: Fluoxetine, paroxetine or bupropion with metoprolol or propranolol
statement: Prescribed fluoxetine, paroxetine, or bupropion - and the patient is co-prescribed metoprolol or propranolol (risk of bradycardia)

plain_summary: Fluoxetine, paroxetine and bupropion can raise the level of metoprolol and propranolol in the body. Together they can slow the heart too much (bradycardia). For fluoxetine with metoprolol, check whether metoprolol is being used for heart failure before supply. If it is, Australian fluoxetine product information lists this combination as contraindicated and the pharmacist should seek prescriber review before supply.

medicine_groups.name: Fluoxetine, paroxetine and bupropion
medicine_groups.note: Zyban is sold for stopping smoking. A supply of it still counts as bupropion. Count combination tablets containing bupropion, including Contrave with naltrexone.

rule_for_models: Suspect a finding when a Group A medicine (fluoxetine, paroxetine or bupropion) and a Group B medicine (metoprolol or propranolol) are both supplied, where supply dates overlap or fall within 60 days of each other. Name both medicines.
cannot_be_seen: Heart rate, ECG and blood pressure results, symptoms such as dizziness or fainting, the doses actually taken, and whether the beta-blocker is used for the heart or for another reason.
ask_the_gp: Could you review the combination, check the heart rate and consider whether an alternative would suit the reason each medicine is used?
